meta.description: Build clinical and healthcare deep-learning pipelines with PyHealth 2.0 covering the complete dataset → task → model → trainer → metrics workflow. Supports EHR datasets (MIMIC-III/IV, eICU, OMOP, EHRShot), signal data (SleepEDF, SHHS, ISRUC), imaging (ChestXray14, COVID19-CXR), clinical prediction tasks (mortality, readmission, length-of-stay, drug recommendation, sleep staging, ICD coding), clinical models (Transformer, RETAIN, GAMENet, SafeDrug, MICRON, StageNet, AdaCare), and medical code utilities (ICD/ATC/NDC/RxNorm lookup and cross-mapping).

scientific_integrity.detail: Strong methodological guidance: split by patient not sample to prevent leakage, match task to dataset, pick monitor metric appropriately

practice_boundaries.detail: Clear scope: clinical/healthcare ML pipelines following dataset → task → model → trainer → metrics pattern; not general PyTorch on tabular data

methodological_ground.detail: Based on PyHealth 2.0 from pyhealth.dev with stable 5-stage pipeline architecture; references established clinical datasets and models

code_usability.detail: Production-ready with <20 line canonical pipeline, copy-pasteable starter, 5 reference files mapping use cases to API modules

functional_suitability.note: Complete clinical ML pipeline: datasets (EHR/signal/imaging), tasks (prediction/recommendation/staging/coding), models (clinical architectures), trainer, metrics, medical codes

reliability.note: Excellent guidance with 'Critical things to get right' section addressing common failures: BaseDataset vs SampleDataset, split leakage, task-dataset matching, monitor selection

performance_context.note: Good optimization guidance: cache_dir for reuse, GPU/CPU tips; SKILL.md 125 lines concise; could expand on multi-GPU/distributed training

agent_usability.note: Outstanding: <20 line canonical pipeline, critical-mistakes section, reference file mapping table, copy-pasteable starter in assets/, 5 focused reference files

human_usability.note: Clear triggers (PyHealth, MIMIC, eICU, EHR, clinical prediction, medical codes), when-to-use section, scope statement about pipeline fit

security.note: Good practices: synthetic MIMIC option for demos, credentialing guidance; minor: MIMIC access requirements could emphasize data use agreements more

maintainability.note: Excellent structure: 5 reference files with clear use-case mapping, version pinning (2.0, Python 3.12-3.14), uv-based reproducible install, starter in assets/

agent_specific.note: Good composability within PyHealth ecosystem; deterministic with fixed seeds; minor: cross-skill integration (with visualization, statistics) could be stronger

inputs.label: MIMIC-III mortality prediction with 5-stage pipeline
inputs.note: Standard clinical prediction workflow with current API

assertions.text: BaseDataset → set_task → SampleDataset → Model pipeline enforced
split_by_patient prevents train/test leakage from same patient
Model initialized with SampleDataset not BaseDataset
assertions.note: Most common error prevented by clear documentation

assertions.text: Trainer with monitor='pr_auc' for binary classification
MIMIC-IV uses ehr_root= not root= parameter
Task must match dataset: MortalityPredictionMIMIC4 not MIMIC3 version
cache_dir recommended for reproducible work
Synthetic MIMIC-III available for demos without credentialing
Drug recommendation models: GAMENet, SafeDrug
Monitor metric: pr_auc_samples or jaccard_samples for multilabel
Wrong monitor saves wrong epoch checkpoint
assertions.note: Consequence of metric mismatch explicitly stated

assertions.text: Task definition in references/tasks.md with dataset mapping
Medical code utilities: ICD-9-CM, ICD-10-CM, ATC, NDC, RxNorm, CCS
Cross-mapping between code systems documented
Reference file references/medcode.md for detailed API
Tokenizers for medical codes included
assertions.note: Complete utility set for code handling

assertions.text: Signal datasets: SleepEDF, SHHS, ISRUC supported
Sleep staging task with multiclass classification
Monitor metrics: accuracy or f1_macro for multiclass
Same 5-stage pipeline applies to signal data
assertions.note: Unified pipeline claimed but signal-specific preprocessing not detailed

inputs.label: Installation with uv and Python version pinning

assertions.text: uv-based installation with Python 3.12-3.14 requirement
uv python pin 3.12 for project-level version locking
Legacy 1.x line available with pyhealth==1.16 for Python 3.9+
Copy-pasteable starter in assets/starter_pipeline.py verified
assertions.note: Referenced but file not verified in directory listing

key_strengths: Outstanding pedagogical structure with 'Critical things to get right' section addressing 6 most common failures before they happen
Excellent unified 5-stage pipeline (dataset → task → model → trainer → metrics) consistently applied across EHR, signal, and imaging modalities
Strong methodological guidance: split by patient to prevent leakage, match task to dataset, select appropriate monitor metric for task type
Comprehensive domain coverage: EHR (MIMIC-III/IV, eICU, OMOP), signals (sleep staging), imaging, with medical code utilities (ICD/ATC/NDC/RxNorm)
Production-ready with <20 line canonical example, copy-pasteable starter, reference file mapping table, uv-based reproducible installation

recommendations.title: Expand signal preprocessing guidance
recommendations.problem: Signal datasets (SleepEDF, SHHS, ISRUC) follow same 5-stage pipeline but signal-specific preprocessing not detailed
recommendations.root_cause: Documentation optimized for EHR workflows which dominate use cases
recommendations.fix: Add references/signal_preprocessing.md covering resampling, filtering, epoching, artifact rejection, channel selection for physiological signals

recommendations.title: Strengthen data use agreement emphasis for MIMIC access
recommendations.problem: MIMIC credentialing mentioned but data use agreement requirements not prominent
recommendations.root_cause: Focus on technical access rather than ethical/legal requirements
recommendations.fix: Add callout in references/installation.md: 'MIMIC datasets require human subjects training and signed data use agreement. Never share MIMIC data or derivatives outside authorized project scope.'
